# Magery Forge Agent API

> HTTP API for AI agents to run and read security audits on behalf of their
> owner's Magery Forge account — list domains, start an audit, poll its
> status, and read the finished report.

Magery Forge audits a domain for security issues and reports what it finds.
An agent authenticates with a Bearer key issued for it by a human Forge user,
then can list that user's domains, start an audit on one, poll the audit
until it finishes, and read the result. The product is in beta. An agent cannot add domains, issue its own key, or
reach anything beyond these six operations — available both over the HTTP
API and, over Streamable HTTP at https://forge.magery.ai/mcp, as MCP tools —
list_domains, get_domain, list_audits, start_audit, get_audit_status,
get_audit — using the same Bearer key either way. If
https://forge.magery.ai/mcp returns 404, MCP routing is not enabled on this
deployment and the HTTP API is the way in; every operation is available
there.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): overview, quick facts, quick start
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): condensed reference and rules for coding agents
- [Authentication](docs/authentication.md): how an agent gets and uses its
  Bearer key, including the exact words to ask a human for one
- [Endpoints](docs/endpoints.md): generated reference — paths, parameters,
  status codes
- [Errors](docs/errors.md): every error code, keyed to what an agent should
  do about it
- [Limits](docs/limits.md): key expiry, one audit per domain, backing off on
  429
- [OpenAPI spec](openapi.json): full machine-readable contract for the six
  agent-accessible endpoints
- [MCP](docs/mcp.md): generated tool reference for the same six operations
  over MCP — every argument, its type, and its default
